mainTopic: Enlarging communal measures, and the rules against hoarding, price-gouging and exporting food from ארץ ישראל.
overview: The גמרא finishes the פסוק in יחזקאל that seems to make a מנה equal sixty שקלים. It learns three rules from it: the holy מנה was double, a community may enlarge measures by up to a sixth, and that sixth is counted as part of the new total. In a story, רב פפא בר שמואל makes a bigger measure and defends it as a brand-new measure. Some towns accepted it and some did not. A memory aid then opens a new topic: protecting the public's food supply and prices. A ברייתא says the נביא עמוס condemns hoarders, lenders who charge רבית, people who cheat on measures, and price-gougers. The גמרא compares how שמואל and his father sold produce and explains why selling early is better. It then sets the limits of the hoarding ban: one's own produce, spices, and the years around שביעית are allowed, but in a drought nothing may be stored. Finally, a ברייתא forbids taking basic foods out of ארץ ישראל, even to סוריא. רבי's lenient view begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A מנה can't be sixty שקלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the פסוק in יחזקאל adds up to sixty שקלים, which is 240 dinars, but a מנה is only 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מנה?! That comes out to two hundred and forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a math problem in the פסוק it just quoted. The numbers in the פסוק total sixty שקלים, which would be 240 dinars, far more than a normal מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מנה is 100 dinars, which is 25 שקלים, since each שקל is 4 dinars. The פסוק in יחזקאל lists 20 + 25 + 15 = 60 שקלים for one מנה. Sixty times four is 240, so the פסוק seems to contradict the known size of a מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of money/weight, normally 100 dinars

phrases.english: A maneh?!
phrases.notes: This refers to the פסוק just quoted (יחזקאל 45:12), whose numbers add up to sixty שקלים.

phrases.english: They are two hundred and forty!
phrases.notes: Sixty שקלים at four dinars each is 240 dinars, but a מנה is only 100.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פסוק from יחזקאל quoted just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in יחזקאל that seems to set a מנה at sixty שקלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sum in the פסוק (60 שקלים = 240 dinars) does not match the known size of a מנה (100 dinars).

steps.title: Three lessons from the פסוק in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the problem by learning three rules from the פסוק: the holy מנה was doubled, measures may be enlarged by up to a sixth, and the sixth is counted from the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn three things from it: the holy מנה was double; we may add to measures, but no more than a sixth; and that sixth is measured from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of treating the פסוק as wrong, the גמרא says the strange number teaches three rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holy מנה was double the regular one: 50 שקלים instead of 25. יחזקאל's 60 means 10 שקלים were added, which teaches that a community may enlarge measures, but only by a limited amount. Those 10 are one sixth of the new total (60), even though they are one fifth of the old amount (50). That is what 'a sixth from the outside' means.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outside, counted as part of the final total

steps.whatToRemember: The holy מנה was double. A community may enlarge measures by up to one sixth, and that sixth is counted as part of the new total, which equals one fifth of the old amount.
steps.confusionAlert: A sixth 'from the outside' does NOT mean adding a sixth of the old amount. It means the added part ends up as a sixth of the new total: 50 + 10 = 60.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule, attributed to שמואל, that the next story is built on.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it three things:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מָנֶה שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ – כָּפוּל הָיָה;
phrases.english: Learn from it that the holy maneh was doubled;
phrases.notes: So the holy מנה was 50 שקלים, not 25.

phrases.english: and learn from it that we may add to the measures,
but we may not add more than one sixth;
and learn from it that the sixth is from the outside.
phrases.notes: The 10 that were added are a sixth of the new 60, though they are a fifth of the old 50.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the math problem by turning it into three rules.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the extra amount is meaningful and teaches rules.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's total of 60 contradicts the size of a regular מנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The holy מנה was 50 שקלים. יחזקאל's 60 shows that measures may be enlarged by up to a sixth of the final total.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל makes a larger measure
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל set up a new measure holding three קפיזי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל instituted a measure of three קפיזי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that tests the one-sixth rule. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The existing measure held two קפיזי. Making it three is an increase of one third, much more than the one-sixth limit just taught.

keyTerms.meaning: A small unit of volume (plural of קְפִיזָא)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel instituted
a measure of three kefizi.
phrases.notes: The usual measure held two, so this is an increase of one third.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל תַּקֵּין כְּיָילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that seems to break the rule from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new measure of three קפיזי was set up.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל's one-sixth limit
steps.stepSummary: The Sages object that שמואל ruled measures may not be enlarged by more than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But שמואל said that we may not add to measures more than a sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: People challenge רב פפא בר שמואל, because his measure seems to break the one-sixth limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going from two to three קפיזי adds a third. That is double the allowed sixth.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say...? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: They said to him: But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הַמִּדּוֹת יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁתוּת!
phrases.english: One may not add to the measures more than a sixth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the action in step 3 using the rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא בר שמואל's three-קפיזי measure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A one-third increase goes beyond שמואל's one-sixth limit.

steps.title: It is a brand-new measure
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל answers that he did not enlarge an old measure but created a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I instituted a new measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא בר שמואל explains that the one-sixth rule does not apply to what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is about enlarging an existing measure. A brand-new measure with its own name and size is not a change to the old one, so the old measure stays as it was.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא כְּיָילָא חַדְתָּא תַּקֵּינִי.
phrases.english: He said to them: I instituted a new measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a new measure, not an enlarged old one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He enlarged the existing measure beyond the limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one-sixth limit applies only to changing an existing measure, not to creating a new one.

steps.title: Some towns accepted the new measure
steps.stepSummary: פומבדיתא rejected the measure, פאפוניא accepted it, and they called it 'רוז פפא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent it to פומבדיתא and they did not accept it; he sent it to פאפוניא and they accepted it, and they called it 'the measure of פפא'.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by telling us how the new measure was received in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new measure only works if a community agrees to use it. One town said no and another said yes, and in that town it was named after רב פפא.

phrases.english: He sent it to Pumbedita, and they did not accept it;
he sent it to Paphunya, and they accepted it;
and they called it "the measure of Pappa."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A new measure may be set up, but it only takes hold where the community accepts it.

steps.title: Memory aid for the coming topics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the order of the next discussions about trade and food supply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: Hoarders of produce; one may not hoard; one may not export; one may not profit; twice with eggs; they sound the alarm; and they may not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is a list of key words that sets up the next several discussions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to a coming teaching, starting with hoarding food. Its job is only to help the learner remember the order of what follows.

keyTerms.meaning: They sound the alarm (blow trumpets in a crisis)

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Hoarders of produce; one may not hoard;
and one may not export; and one may not profit;
twice with eggs; they sound the alarm; and one may not leave.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new topic: dishonest and harmful business practices.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This only lists the topics to come.

steps.title: Four kinds of cheaters condemned by the prophet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that hoarders, lenders who charge רבית, people who shrink measures, and price-gougers are the ones עמוס speaks about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: hoarders of produce, lenders with interest, those who shrink the איפה, and those who raise prices — about them the פסוק says: 'Saying, when will the new month pass so we can sell grain, and the שבת so we can open up the grain, making the איפה small and the שקל big, and twisting the scales of deceit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing four kinds of people who take advantage of others with food and money. It ties them to a פסוק in עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes people who can't wait for holy days to end so they can get back to selling and cheating. Its phrases fit the list: shrinking the איפה (cheating on measures), enlarging the שקל (charging more), and rigged scales.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who make the measure smaller

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that cheating in the marketplace is treated as a serious sin, condemned by a נביא.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אוֹצְרֵי פֵירוֹת, וּמַלְוֵי בְּרִבִּית,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Hoarders of produce, and lenders with interest,
and those who shrink the eifah, and those who raise prices —
phrases.notes: An איפה is a measuring container. 'Shrinking' it means giving buyers less than they paid for.

phrases.english: about them the verse says:
"Saying: When will the new month pass, so we may sell grain,
and the Shabbat, so we may open up grain,
making the eifah small and the shekel big,
and twisting the scales of deceit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the first topic named in the memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hoarders, lenders with interest, measure-cheaters and price-gougers are the people condemned in עמוס 8:5.

steps.title: God swears never to forget their deeds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a second פסוק showing how severe this sin is: ה׳ swears never to forget what they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'ה׳ has sworn by the pride of יעקב: I will never forget any of their deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another פסוק to show how serious these sins are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק described what these people do. This פסוק describes the result: ה׳ swears never to forget their actions, which shows how harsh their punishment is.
steps.whatToRemember: Cheating people on food, loans, measures and prices is condemned by the נביא‎. ה׳ swears never to forget it.

phrases.english: And it is written: "The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob:
I will never forget any of their deeds."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to the same ברייתא to show the punishment.
steps.raayaObject: How severe the sin of the four cheaters in step 8 is.

steps.title: Who is an example of a produce hoarder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real-life example of the 'hoarders of produce' listed in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hoarders of produce: who is an example of this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 8 and asks who is an example of an אוצר פירות. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed hoarders as people that עמוס criticized, but it gave no example. The גמרא wants a concrete picture of what this sin looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: Hoarders of produce: people who buy up food and store it to raise prices
Such as whom? A request for an example

phrases.english: Hoarders of produce:
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the ברייתא in step 8, the list of people עמוס criticizes.

phrases.english: such as whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first item in the ברייתא's list and asks for an example
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of who is meant by 'hoarders of produce'

steps.title: שבתי the hoarder
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a known hoarder named שבתי is the example.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Such as שבתי, the hoarder of produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers with a real person, שבתי, who was famous for hoarding produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a definition, רבי יוחנן points to a well-known person. Everyone knew שבתי bought up large amounts of food and held it to sell at high prices, so his name was the clearest example.

keyTerms.meaning: שבתי the produce hoarder, a person famous for this practice

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Such as Shabbtai, the hoarder of produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן שַׁבְּתַי אַצָּר פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The model hoarder is שבתי, who bought produce to store and sell later at high prices

steps.title: How שמואל's father and שמואל sold produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how אבוה דשמואל sold early at the cheap price, while שמואל held his produce and sold later, but still at the cheap price.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבוה דשמואל would sell produce in the early, cheap season at the cheap price. His son שמואל would hold the produce and sell it in the late, expensive season, but at the cheap early price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story comparing two honest ways of selling food. This story sets up the ruling from ארץ ישראל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither of them overcharged: both sold at the low, early price. The only difference is timing. The father sold right away, while שמואל waited until food was scarce and then sold cheaply to help people when they needed it most.

keyTerms.meaning: The early market price, when produce is plentiful and cheap
The late market price, when produce is scarce and expensive

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל was NOT a hoarder who raised prices. He held the produce but sold it at the cheap price. The question is only which way helps the public more.

phrases.english: Shmuel's father would sell produce
during the early price season, for the early price.
Shmuel his son would hold the produce,
and sell it during the late price season,
for the early price.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining bad hoarding, the גמרא shows two honest selling practices to compare
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sold at the low price; the father sold early, שמואל sold late

steps.title: The father's way is better
steps.stepSummary: Sages in ארץ ישראל sent a message that the father's practice is better than the son's.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there (ארץ ישראל): The father's way is better than the son's.
steps.whatsHappening: The sages of ארץ ישראל judge between the two practices and say the father's way is better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, since שמואל helped people at the hardest time. The ruling tells us that selling early has a bigger benefit, and the גמרא will explain why in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, a message from the sages of ארץ ישראל
The father's (way) is better than the son's

phrases.english: They sent from there:
The father's is better than the son's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a verdict on the two practices described in step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Selling early at the cheap price is better than holding and selling cheaply later

steps.title: Why is the father's way better?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ruling from ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the father's way is better. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל seemed to help people more at the time of need, the ruling needs an explanation.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why selling early is better than holding and selling cheaply later

steps.title: A low price stays low
steps.stepSummary: A market price that starts low stays low, so selling early keeps prices down the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: A price that has eased stays eased.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that when prices start low, they tend to stay low all year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By selling early, the father pushed the whole market price down at the start, and it stayed down for everyone. שמואל only helped those who bought from him, while the general market price had already gone up.
steps.whatToRemember: Selling early at a low price helps the whole market all year, because a price that starts low stays low.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the goal is to help the public's market price, not just to give individual buyers a good deal.

phrases.english: A price that has eased stays eased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An early low price keeps the whole market low all year

steps.title: A person may store his own produce
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a person may store produce from his own field without breaking the hoarding rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A person may make his own kav into a storehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a rule: storing your own produce is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on hoarding is about buying up food from the market. Keeping what you grew yourself does not take food away from the public market in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: His קב, a measure of produce; here it means his own produce

phrases.english: Rav said:
A person may make his own kav into a storehouse.
phrases.notes: He means a person may store the produce of his own field and sell it later.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: עוֹשֶׂה אָדָם אֶת קַבּוֹ אוֹצָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the ban against hoarding discussed earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Storing produce from one's own field is permitted

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says hoarding is forbidden only for basic foods bought from the market, but allowed for spices and for one's own produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: One may not hoard basic foods, like wine, oil, and flour. But spices, like cumin and pepper, are allowed. This applies to someone who buys from the market, but someone bringing in his own produce is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two limits on the hoarding ban. First, it applies only to basic foods people need to live, not spices. Second, it applies only to food bought from the market, which is exactly רב's point.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the previous statement)
Basic needs for life, essential food

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One may not hoard produce
of things that are basic to life,
such as wines, oils, and flours.
But spices, cumin and pepper, are permitted.
When is this said?
For one who buys from the market,
but one who brings in his own produce is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's statement in step 16
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that one may store his own produce
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forbids hoarding only for food bought from the market

steps.title: Hoarding is allowed in the years around שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that in ארץ ישראל, one may store produce for three years: the year before שביעית, שביעית itself, and the year after.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a person may store produce in ארץ ישראל for three years: the year before שביעית, שביעית, and the year after שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with another case where storing food is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During שביעית the land is not farmed, so food from the sixth year must last a long time. Storing food then is not cheating the public; it is a real need.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, when the land rests

steps.whatToRemember: The hoarding ban has limits: it does not apply to spices, to one's own produce, or to the years around שביעית in ארץ ישראל. But the next step adds that in drought years no storing at all is allowed.

phrases.english: And it is permitted for a person to store produce
in Eretz Yisrael for three years:
the year before the Sabbatical Year, the Sabbatical Year, and the year after the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוּתָּר לָאָדָם לֶאֱצוֹר פֵּירוֹת בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another permitted case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, storing produce is allowed during the year before, during, and after שביעית

steps.title: In drought years, no storing at all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that in years of drought, a person may not store even a קב of carobs, because it hurts market prices.
steps.simpleTranslation: In years of drought, a person may not store even a small amount of carobs, because he brings a curse on the market prices.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step continues. It adds a limit: in a drought year, all storing is forbidden, even a tiny amount of a cheap food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, storing was allowed for one's own produce, and in ארץ ישראל for three years around שביעית. Now the ברייתא says that a drought changes things. When food is scarce, people panic, and even a small hoard can push prices up for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Years of drought, when food is scarce
Carobs, a cheap and simple food

steps.confusionAlert: The word שְּׁעָרִים here does not mean 'gates.' It means market prices.

phrases.english: And in years of drought –
one may not store even a kav of carobs,
because he brings a curse on the market prices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and limits the storage permissions given in Steps 17-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In years of drought, storing any amount of food is forbidden, even a קב of carobs.

steps.title: A sage stores three years of produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא tells his servant פוגא to store produce for him for three years around שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said to his servant פוגא: Go store produce for me for three years: the year before שביעית, שביעית, and the year after שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing a sage actually using the three-year storage permission from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 18 said that in ארץ ישראל one may store for three years around שביעית. Here a real sage living in ארץ ישראל does exactly that. This shows the rule was followed in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
to Fuga, his servant:
Go, store produce for me
for three years –
the year before the Sabbatical Year, the Sabbatical Year, and the year after the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְפוּגָא שַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the three-year storage rule from Step 18 being used in real life.
steps.raayaObject: The permission to store produce for three years around שביעית in ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who told his servant to store produce for those three years

steps.title: No taking basic foods out of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that basic foods like wine, oil and flour may not be taken out of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One may not take produce out of ארץ ישראל if it is a basic food that keeps people alive, such as wines, oils and fine flours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא on a related topic: taking basic foods out of ארץ ישראל is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits with the rules about storing. Both are about keeping basic food available and cheap for the people of ארץ ישראל. Sending food out of the land leaves less at home and raises prices there.

keyTerms.meaning: Basic foods that keep people alive

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not take produce out of Eretz Yisrael –
items that are basic foods that keep people alive,
such as wines, oils, and fine flours.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין פֵּירוֹת מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new but related topic. The last steps were about storing food, and this one is about taking food out of the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Basic foods such as wine, oil and flour may not be taken out of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא allows exporting wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא permits taking wine out of the land, because less wine means less wild behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא permits taking out wine, because doing so reduces immoral behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא disagrees about one item on the list. He says wine may be taken out of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion counted wine as a basic food. רבי יהודה בן בתירא gives another reason: wine can lead people to wild, immoral behavior. So having less wine in the land is actually a good thing, and he allows it to be sent out.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא מַתִּיר בַּיַּיִן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira permits it with wine,
because it reduces immoral behavior.
phrases.notes: Too much wine can lead to wild behavior, so sending some away means less of that at home.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא מַתִּיר בַּיַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion about wine, one of the items listed in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה בן בתירא, wine may be taken out of ארץ ישראל because it reduces immoral behavior.

steps.title: The ban includes taking food to סוריא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the ban on taking food out of ארץ ישראל also covers taking it to סוריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as one may not take food from ארץ ישראל to outside the land, so too one may not take it from ארץ ישראל to סוריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spreads the ban to one more place: סוריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think סוריא, which is close to ארץ ישראל, is treated like part of the land. The ברייתא says no. For this rule, it counts like outside the land, so taking food there is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, the area next to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And just as one may not take out
from the Land to outside the Land,
so too one may not take out
from Eretz Yisrael to Syria.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מוֹצִיאִין מֵאֶרֶץ לְחוּץ לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the ban from Step 21 to include סוריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Basic foods may not be taken from ארץ ישראל to סוריא either.

steps.title: רבי begins a lenient opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי starts to say that he permits something about taking food out. His words continue in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי permits...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move: רבי is about to disagree and allow something. The rest of his opinion comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the ברייתא forbids taking food to סוריא, רבי opens with 'permits.' So he is about to give a more lenient view on the ban. Exactly what he permits is explained in the words that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: And Rabbi permits

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts רבי's more lenient opinion on the export ban from Steps 21-23. What exactly he permits comes in the continuation of the ברייתא on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי takes a lenient position. The details continue in the next section.
